entities.summary: Jean Petit was a French theologian and professor in the University of Paris, known for his public defence of a political killing as tyrannicide. Born in 1385, Petit was a prominent figure in the University's theology department, where he taught and debated with prominent thinkers of the time. His views on the legitimacy of killing tyrants in the name of God earned him both praise and controversy. Petit's most notable defence was of a French nobleman who had been killed in a political assassination, with Petit arguing that the killing was justified as an act of tyrannicide. This stance put Petit at odds with some of his colleagues, but also earned him recognition as a defender of the faith. Petit's legacy as a defender of the faith and his advocacy for the use of force against tyrants have made him a fascinating figure in the history of French theology. His writings on the subject continue to be studied by scholars today. Petit's commitment to his beliefs and his willingness to challenge conventional wisdom have made him a lasting figure in the annals of French intellectual history.
